name: Gorkha Durbar
deity: Gorakhkali and Kalika (temples within the palace); Gorakhnath (cave shrine)
built_century_text: Built by King Ram Shah of Gorkha; Wikipedia dates it to the 16th century while other sources place Ram Shah's reign in the 17th century. The Kalika temple inside is dated to the 17th century.
architecture: Fortified hilltop palace in Newar style, built mainly of brick, stone and timber. Walls are about three feet thick, floors rest on projecting wooden beams, and the wings rise over several levels with carved windows and struts. The Kalika temple has wood carvings of birds, animals and deities.
short: Hilltop fortress-palace of the Shah kings of Gorkha and birthplace of Prithvi Narayan Shah, unifier of Nepal.
story: Catch your breath: you have climbed to a ridge about a thousand metres high, and the fortified palace in front of you is where modern Nepal began. King Ram Shah of Gorkha built this durbar, and in 1723 Prithvi Narayan Shah was born here, in the part called Dhuni Pati. From these walls, some three feet thick, he set out on the campaigns that unified Nepal. Look at the carved windows and the timber beams that carry the floors; Newar craftsmen from the valley shaped them. Inside the compound stand the temples of Kalika and Gorakhkali, and nearby is the cave where the yogi Gorakhnath is said to have meditated, which draws a fair every Baisakh Purnima. To the south burns the eternal flame, kept alight since unification. Now turn north. On a clear day Manaslu, Himalchuli, Annapurna and Ganesh Himal line the horizon. The 2015 earthquake damaged the palace, and restoration work by the Department of Archaeology began in November 2017.
legend: The cave below the palace is believed to be the place where the yogi Gorakhnath, a disciple of Matsyendranath, sheltered and meditated; the Gorkha kingdom and the Gorkhali people take their name from him.
facts: Prithvi Narayan Shah, who began the unification of Nepal, was born in the palace in 1723.
The palace sits on a hilltop at about 1,000 m, roughly an hour's walk from Gorkha bazaar.
Its walls are about three feet thick and its floors are carried on extended wooden beams.
UNESCO has listed 'The medieval palace complex of Gorkha' on Nepal's Tentative List since 1996.
Reconstruction after the 2015 earthquake began on 15 November 2017 under the Department of Archaeology.

visit.hours_note: Reached by a steep stone stairway (about an hour on foot) from Gorkha bazaar. Opening hours not confirmed in a reliable source.
visit.fee_note: No current official fee schedule found; check at the gate. Visitor numbers come from the Gorkha Museum.

earthquake_2015: The April 2015 earthquake partially damaged the palace. Reconstruction by the Department of Archaeology started on 15 November 2017 and was still ongoing in 2022.

quiz.q: Which future king was born in Gorkha Durbar in 1723?
quiz.explanation: Prithvi Narayan Shah, who began the unification of Nepal, was born in the palace's Dhuni Pati in 1723.
quiz.q_np: सन् 1723 मा गोरखा दरबारमा जन्मिएका भावी राजा को थिए?
quiz.explanation_np: नेपाल एकीकरण सुरु गर्ने पृथ्वीनारायण शाह सन् 1723 मा दरबारको धुनीपाटीमा जन्मिएका थिए।

quiz.q: Which yogi gives his name to the cave shrine near the palace?
quiz.explanation: The cave is believed to be where Gorakhnath meditated; a fair is held there on Baisakh Purnima.
quiz.q_np: दरबार नजिकैको गुफा मन्दिरले कुन योगीको नाम बोकेको छ?
quiz.explanation_np: यो गुफामा गोरखनाथले तपस्या गरेको विश्वास गरिन्छ; बैशाख पूर्णिमामा यहाँ मेला लाग्छ।

quiz.q: About how thick are the palace walls?
quiz.explanation: The walls of the fortified palace are about three feet thick.
quiz.q_np: दरबारका भित्ताहरू करिब कति बाक्लो छन्?
quiz.explanation_np: किल्लाजस्तो दरबारका भित्ताहरू करिब तीन फिट बाक्लो छन्।

quiz.q: Which Himalayan peaks can be seen to the north from the palace?
quiz.explanation: The palace is a viewpoint for Manaslu, Himalchuli, Annapurna and Ganesh peaks.
quiz.q_np: दरबारबाट उत्तरतर्फ कुन हिमालका चुचुरा देखिन्छन्?
quiz.explanation_np: दरबार मनास्लु, हिमालचुली, अन्नपूर्ण र गणेश हिमाल हेर्ने स्थान हो।

quiz.q: Under what name is the site on Nepal's UNESCO Tentative List?
options: The medieval palace complex of Gorkha
quiz.explanation: It was added in 1996 as 'The medieval palace complex of Gorkha' (reference 842).
quiz.q_np: नेपालको युनेस्को अस्थायी सूचीमा यो स्थल कुन नामले छ?
quiz.explanation_np: यसलाई सन् 1996 मा ‘गोरखाको मध्यकालीन दरबार परिसर’ (सन्दर्भ 842) नामले थपिएको थियो।

clues: A king who joined many small states into one nation was born behind my thick walls on a mountain ridge.
Climb my long stairway and a goddess temple, a yogi's cave and a flame that never goes out are waiting at the top.

festivals.name: Baisakh Purnima fair
festivals.note: Annual fair held on the full-moon day of Baisakh at the Gorakhnath cave near the palace.
festivals.note_np: दरबार नजिकैको गोरखनाथ गुफामा बैशाख महिनाको पूर्णिमाका दिन लाग्ने वार्षिक मेला।

short_np: गोरखाका शाह राजाहरूको डाँडामाथिको किल्ला-दरबार र नेपाल एकीकरण गर्ने पृथ्वीनारायण शाहको जन्मस्थल।
story_np: सास फेर्नुहोस्: तपाईं करिब एक हजार मिटर अग्लो चुचुरोमा पुग्नुभएको छ, र तपाईंको अगाडि रहेको किल्लाबन्द दरबार नै आधुनिक नेपालको सुरुवात भएको ठाउँ हो। गोरखाका राजा राम शाहले यो दरबार बनाए, र 1723 मा यहीँ, धुनी पाटी भनिने भागमा, पृथ्वीनारायण शाहको जन्म भयो। करिब तीन फिट बाक्लो यिनै पर्खालबाट उनी नेपाल एकीकरण गर्ने अभियानमा निस्किए। कुँदिएका झ्याल र भुइँ थाम्ने काठका धरनहरू हेर्नुहोस्; ती उपत्यकाका नेवार शिल्पीहरूले बनाएका हुन्। परिसरभित्र कालिका र गोरखकालीका मन्दिर छन्, र नजिकै योगी गोरखनाथले ध्यान गरेको भनिने गुफा छ, जहाँ हरेक वैशाख पूर्णिमामा मेला लाग्छ। दक्षिणतिर एकीकरणदेखि निरन्तर बलिरहेको अखण्ड ज्योति छ। अब उत्तरतिर फर्कनुहोस्। खुला दिनमा मनास्लु, हिमालचुली, अन्नपूर्ण र गणेश हिमाल क्षितिजमा लाइन लागेर देखिन्छन्। 2015 को भूकम्पले दरबारमा क्षति पुर्‍यायो, र पुरातत्त्व विभागले नोभेम्बर 2017 मा पुनर्निर्माण कार्य सुरु गर्‍यो।
legend_np: दरबारमुनिको गुफा मत्स्येन्द्रनाथका शिष्य योगी गोरखनाथले आश्रय लिएर ध्यान गरेको स्थान मानिन्छ; गोरखा राज्य र गोरखाली जातिले उनैबाट नाम पाएका हुन्।
facts_np: नेपाल एकीकरण अभियान सुरु गर्ने पृथ्वीनारायण शाहको जन्म 1723 मा यही दरबारमा भएको थियो।
दरबार करिब 1,000 मिटर उचाइको डाँडामा छ, गोरखा बजारबाट करिब एक घण्टाको पैदल दूरीमा।
यसका पर्खाल करिब तीन फिट बाक्लो छन् र भुइँहरू बाहिर निस्किएका काठका धरनमा अडिएका छन्।
युनेस्कोले 1996 देखि 'गोरखाको मध्यकालीन दरबार परिसर' लाई नेपालको अस्थायी सूचीमा राखेको छ।
2015 को भूकम्पपछिको पुनर्निर्माण पुरातत्त्व विभागको नेतृत्वमा 15 नोभेम्बर 2017 मा सुरु भएको थियो।
quake_np: सन् 2015 अप्रिलको भूकम्पले दरबारलाई आंशिक क्षति पुर्‍यायो। पुरातत्त्व विभागद्वारा पुनर्निर्माण 15 नोभेम्बर 2017 मा सुरु भयो र 2022 मा पनि जारी थियो।
clues_np: धेरै साना राज्यलाई जोडेर एक राष्ट्र बनाउने राजा पहाडको डाँडामाथिका मेरा बाक्लो भित्ताभित्र जन्मिएका थिए।
मेरो लामो भ्याङ्ग चढ्दै जाऊ; माथि देवी मन्दिर, योगीको गुफा र कहिल्यै नबुझिने ज्वाला तिमीलाई पर्खिरहेका छन्।

name: Manakamana Temple
deity: Goddess Bhagawati (Manakamana), regarded as an incarnation of Lakshmi
built_century_text: Founded in 1678 according to Wikipedia; tradition places its origin in the 17th century under the Gorkha kings Ram Shah or Prithvipati Shah. Rebuilt and gilded between June 2015 and September 2018.
architecture: Two-storey Nepalese pagoda with an ambulatory around the sanctum, carved timber struts and windows. After the 2018 restoration, the roof, door, finial and windows were gold-plated with about 14 kg of gold; limestone, surkhi, brick and wood were used.
short: Hilltop pagoda of the wish-fulfilling goddess above the Trishuli and Marsyangdi rivers, famous for its cable car.
story: Welcome to Kafakdada hill, 1,300 metres above the meeting of the Trishuli and Marsyangdi rivers. The name of this temple is its promise: mana means heart and kamana means wish, and pilgrims believe the goddess Bhagawati grants the wishes of the faithful. The story goes back to the 17th century and the Gorkha court. The queen, it is said, had divine powers known only to her Magar priest, Lakhan Thapa. After the king died and she followed him onto the funeral pyre, she promised to return. Months later a farmer's plough split a stone that ran with blood and milk, and Lakhan Thapa built a shrine on that spot. To this day the priest must be his descendant. Look up at the two-tiered roof: after the 2015 earthquake tilted the temple, restorers gilded its roof, door and windows with about fourteen kilograms of gold. Before 1998 pilgrims walked for three hours; now the cable car lifts you in about ten minutes.
legend: A Gorkha queen with secret divine powers committed sati after her husband's death, promising her priest Lakhan Thapa Magar she would reappear. Six months later a farmer split a stone that poured blood and milk; Lakhan Thapa's rituals stopped the flow and he built the shrine there.
facts: The temple stands at about 1,300 m on Kafakdada hill in Shahid Lakhan Rural Municipality, Gorkha.
By tradition the priest must be a Magar descendant of Lakhan Thapa.
Prithvi Narayan Shah set up a trust in 1764-65 to worship Manakamana and feed the pigeons every day.
The Manakamana cable car, opened on 24 November 1998, runs 2.8 km from Kurintar in about 10 minutes.
After the 2015 earthquake the temple was rebuilt and gold-plated, work finishing in September 2018.

visit.hours_note: Temple hours not confirmed in a reliable source. The cable car usually runs about 9:00-17:00 with a lunch break from noon to 13:30 (Wikipedia).
visit.fee_note: No separate temple entry fee found; the cable car from Kurintar is ticketed separately.

earthquake_2015: The April 2015 earthquake cracked the roof and tilted the temple 9-12 inches to the north-east. Reconstruction under the Department of Archaeology began in June 2015 and was finished in September 2018, costing about NPR 130-140 million.

quiz.q: What does the name Manakamana mean?
quiz.explanation: Mana means heart and kamana means wish; the goddess is believed to grant devotees' wishes.
quiz.q_np: मनकामना नामको अर्थ के हो?
quiz.explanation_np: मन भनेको हृदय र कामना भनेको इच्छा; देवीले भक्तजनका इच्छा पूरा गर्छिन् भन्ने विश्वास छ।

quiz.q: Since 1998, how do most pilgrims reach the temple from Kurintar?
quiz.explanation: The Manakamana cable car opened on 24 November 1998 and covers 2.8 km in about 10 minutes.
quiz.q_np: 1998 देखि धेरैजसो तीर्थयात्री कुरिनटारबाट मन्दिर कसरी पुग्छन्?
quiz.explanation_np: मनकामना केबलकार 24 नोभेम्बर 1998 मा सञ्चालनमा आयो र 2.8 कि.मि. दूरी करिब 10 मिनेटमा पार गर्छ।

quiz.q: By tradition, the temple priest must descend from which person?
quiz.explanation: The priest must be a descendant of Lakhan Thapa Magar, who founded the shrine.
quiz.q_np: परम्परा अनुसार मन्दिरका पुजारी कसका सन्तान हुनुपर्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: पुजारी यस मन्दिरका स्थापक लखन थापा मगरका सन्तान हुनुपर्छ।

quiz.q: Between which two rivers does Kafakdada hill rise?
quiz.explanation: The temple sits on Kafakdada hill at the confluence of the Trishuli and Marsyangdi.
quiz.q_np: काफकदाँडा कुन दुई नदीको बीचमा उठेको छ?
quiz.explanation_np: मन्दिर त्रिशूली र मर्स्याङ्दीको सङ्गमस्थलमा काफकदाँडामा अवस्थित छ।

quiz.q: About how much gold was used to plate the roof, door, finial and windows during the 2015-2018 restoration?
quiz.explanation: About 14 kg of gold, costing around NPR 90 million, was used.
quiz.q_np: 2015-2018 को जीर्णोद्धारमा छाना, ढोका, गजुर र झ्यालमा करिब कति सुन चढाइएको थियो?
quiz.explanation_np: करिब 14 केजी सुन प्रयोग गरियो, जसको लागत करिब नेपाली रुपैयाँ 9 करोड थियो।

clues: My name joins the heart and the wish, and a gondola carries people up to my golden roof.
A stone that bled milk in a farmer's field led a Magar priest to build my shrine above two meeting rivers.

model.notes: Compact two-tier pagoda with fully gilded roofs and dark carved timber, ringed by a railing and crowds, on a paved hilltop with a cable-car station nearby.

short_np: त्रिशूली र मर्स्याङ्दी नदीमाथि इच्छा पूरा गर्ने देवीको डाँडामाथिको पगोडा, केबुलकारका लागि प्रसिद्ध।
story_np: त्रिशूली र मर्स्याङ्दी नदीको सङ्गमभन्दा 1,300 मिटर माथि रहेको काफकडाँडामा स्वागत छ। यस मन्दिरको नामले नै यसको वचन बताउँछ: मन भनेको हृदय र कामना भनेको इच्छा हो, र तीर्थयात्रीहरू विश्वास गर्छन् कि देवी भगवतीले भक्तजनका इच्छा पूरा गर्छिन्। कथा सत्रौँ शताब्दी र गोरखा दरबारसम्म पुग्छ। भनिन्छ, रानीसँग दैवी शक्ति थियो, जुन उनका मगर पुजारी लखन थापालाई मात्र थाहा थियो। राजाको मृत्यु भएपछि रानी उनीसँगै चितामा सती गइन्, र फर्किने वचन दिइन्। महिनौँपछि एक किसानको हलोले एउटा ढुङ्गा चिर्‍यो जसबाट रगत र दूध बग्यो, र लखन थापाले त्यही ठाउँमा मन्दिर बनाए। आजसम्म पुजारी उनै वंशज हुनुपर्छ। दुई तले छानातिर हेर्नुहोस्: सन् 2015 को भूकम्पले मन्दिरलाई ढल्काएपछि पुनर्निर्माणकर्ताहरूले छाना, ढोका र झ्यालहरू करिब चौध किलोग्राम सुनले सजाए। सन् 1998 अघि तीर्थयात्रीहरू तीन घण्टा हिँड्थे; अब केबुलकारले तपाईंलाई करिब दश मिनेटमा माथि पुर्‍याउँछ।
legend_np: गोरखाकी एक रानी, जससँग गोप्य दैवी शक्ति थियो, पतिको मृत्यु भएपछि सती गइन् र आफ्ना पुजारी लखन थापा मगरलाई पुनः देखा पर्ने वचन दिइन्। छ महिनापछि एक किसानले ढुङ्गा चिर्दा त्यसबाट रगत र दूध बग्यो; लखन थापाको अनुष्ठानले त्यो बग्न रोक्यो र उनले त्यहीँ मन्दिर बनाए।
facts_np: मन्दिर गोरखाको शहीद लखन गाउँपालिकामा काफकडाँडामा करिब 1,300 मिटरमा अवस्थित छ।
परम्परा अनुसार पुजारी लखन थापाका मगर वंशज नै हुनुपर्छ।
पृथ्वीनारायण शाहले सन् 1764-65 मा मनकामनाको पूजा गर्न र हरेक दिन परेवालाई दाना खुवाउन गुठी स्थापना गरे।
सन् 1998 को नोभेम्बर 24 मा सञ्चालनमा आएको मनकामना केबुलकार कुरिन्टारबाट 2.8 कि.मि. करिब 10 मिनेटमा चल्छ।
सन् 2015 को भूकम्पपछि मन्दिर पुनर्निर्माण गरी सुनले मोहोरिएको थियो, काम सन् 2018 को सेप्टेम्बरमा सकियो।
quake_np: सन् 2015 को अप्रिलको भूकम्पले छानामा दरार पारेको थियो र मन्दिरलाई उत्तरपूर्वतर्फ 9-12 इन्च ढल्काएको थियो। पुरातत्त्व विभागअन्तर्गतको पुनर्निर्माण सन् 2015 को जुनमा सुरु भई सन् 2018 को सेप्टेम्बरमा सकियो, जसमा करिब रु. 130-140 मिलियन खर्च भयो।
clues_np: मेरो नामले मन र कामनालाई जोड्छ, र एउटा केबलकारले मानिसलाई मेरो सुनौलो छानासम्म पुर्‍याउँछ।
एक किसानको खेतमा दूध बगाएको ढुङ्गाले एक मगर पुजारीलाई दुई नदी मिल्ने ठाउँमाथि मेरो मन्दिर बनाउन डोर्‍यायो।

name: Muktinath Temple
built_century_text: Present shrine built in 1814 or 1815 and credited to Queen Subarna Prabha Devi of Nepal; tradition says it replaced an earlier clay temple built by the kings of Jumla. The site itself is mentioned in the Vishnu Purana's Gandaki Mahatmya.
architecture: Small Newar-style pagoda with a three-tiered roof crowned by a golden brass pinnacle, standing in a courtyard enclosed by 108 bull-headed water spouts (Mukti Dhara) of copper or brass, inside a sacred poplar grove.
short: One of the world's highest temples, at 3,800 m, sacred to Hindus as Vishnu's abode and to Buddhists as Chumig Gyatsa.
story: You have reached 3,800 metres, at the foot of the Thorong La pass, and the air is thin and cold. This is Muktinath, the Lord of Liberation, and both Hindus and Buddhists have walked here for centuries. Hindus come to Vishnu, who is said to have revealed himself here; it is one of the 108 Divya Desams of the Sri Vaishnava tradition and one of Nepal's Char Dham. Buddhists know the place as Chumig Gyatsa, the Hundred Springs, linked with Avalokiteshvara and with Padmasambhava. The small pagoda in front of you, with its three-tiered roof and golden pinnacle, was built around 1815 and is credited to Queen Subarna Prabha Devi. Now walk around it. One hundred and eight bull-headed spouts pour icy water, and brave pilgrims run beneath every one. Nearby, at the Jwala Mai shrine, a small flame burns on natural gas from the earth, so fire and water meet in one holy place.
legend: The poplar trees of the sacred grove are said to have grown from the staffs of the eighty-four siddhas who passed through on their way to Tibet. Buddhists hold that Padmasambhava left a statue of himself at the Mharme Lhakhang Gompa before departing for Tibet.
facts: At about 3,800 m, Muktinath is one of the world's highest temples.
Its courtyard is enclosed by 108 water spouts shaped like bull heads, called the Mukti Dhara.
It is counted among the 108 Divya Desam of Sri Vaishnavism and among the 51 Shakta pithas.
Tibetan Buddhists call it Chumig Gyatsa, the 'Hundred Waters'.
The nearby Jwala Mai temple shelters a flame fed by natural gas from the ground.

visit.hours_note: High-altitude site reached by road or trail from Jomsom via Ranipauwa; opening hours not confirmed in a reliable source.
visit.fee_note: No temple entry fee found. Muktinath lies in the Annapurna Conservation Area, which requires a separate permit for foreign visitors.

quiz.explanation: The 1814-15 construction is credited to Queen Subarna Prabha Devi, who made a pilgrimage around 1807.
quiz.q_np: लगभग 1815 मा वर्तमान मन्दिर बनाउने श्रेय कुन रानीलाई दिइन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: 1814-15 को निर्माणको श्रेय रानी सुवर्ण प्रभा देवीलाई दिइन्छ, जसले करिब 1807 मा तीर्थयात्रा गरेकी थिइन्।

quiz.explanation_np: मुक्तिनाथ थोरङ ला भञ्ज्याङको फेदमा पर्छ।

short_np: विश्वका सबैभन्दा अग्ला मन्दिरमध्ये एक, ३,८०० मिटरमा, हिन्दूहरूका लागि विष्णुको वासस्थान र बौद्धहरूका लागि छुमिग ज्ञाछा।
story_np: तपाईं थोराङ ला भञ्ज्याङको फेदमा ३,८०० मिटरमा पुग्नुभएको छ, र हावा पातलो र चिसो छ। यो मुक्तिनाथ हो, मुक्तिका स्वामी, जहाँ शताब्दीयौंदेखि हिन्दू र बौद्ध दुवै हिँडेर आउँछन्। हिन्दूहरू विष्णुकहाँ आउँछन्, जो यहीँ प्रकट भएका भनिन्छ; यो श्री वैष्णव परम्पराका १०८ दिव्य देशमध्ये एक र नेपालका चार धाममध्ये एक हो। बौद्धहरू यस ठाउँलाई छुमिग ज्ञाछा, अर्थात् सय धारा, भन्छन्, जसलाई अवलोकितेश्वर र पद्मसम्भवसँग जोडिन्छ। तपाईंको अगाडि रहेको तीन तले छाना र सुनौलो गजुर भएको सानो पगोडा सन् १८१५ तिर बनेको हो र रानी सुवर्ण प्रभा देवीलाई श्रेय दिइन्छ। अब यसको वरिपरि घुम्नुहोस्। एक सय आठ वटा गोरुको टाउको आकारका धाराबाट चिसो पानी बग्छ, र साहसी तीर्थयात्रीहरू हरेक धारामुनि दगुरेर नुहाउँछन्। नजिकै ज्वाला माईको मन्दिरमा धर्तीबाट आएको प्राकृतिक ग्यासले सानो ज्योति बलिरहन्छ, यसरी एउटै पवित्र स्थानमा आगो र पानी भेट्छन्।
legend_np: पवित्र वनका पपलर रुखहरू तिब्बततर्फ जाँदै गर्दा यहाँ भएर गएका चौरासी सिद्धहरूका लट्ठीबाट उम्रेका भनिन्छ। बौद्धहरूको विश्वासअनुसार पद्मसम्भवले तिब्बत जानुअघि म्हार्मे ल्हाखाङ गुम्बामा आफ्नो एउटा मूर्ति छाडेका थिए।
facts_np: करिब ३,८०० मिटरमा रहेको मुक्तिनाथ विश्वका सबैभन्दा अग्ला मन्दिरहरूमध्ये एक हो।
यसको आँगन गोरुको टाउको आकारका १०८ पानीका धाराले घेरिएको छ, जसलाई मुक्ति धारा भनिन्छ।
यो श्री वैष्णव सम्प्रदायका १०८ दिव्य देशमध्ये र ५१ शक्तिपीठमध्ये गनिन्छ।
तिब्बती बौद्धहरू यसलाई छुमिग ज्ञाछा, 'सय पानी', भन्छन्।
नजिकैको ज्वाला माई मन्दिरमा जमिनबाट आउने प्राकृतिक ग्यासले बलेको ज्योति रहेको छ।
clues_np: सुक्खा हिमाली उपत्यकामा अवस्थित यहाँ तीर्थयात्रीहरू एक सय आठ चिसा धाराहरूमा दौडिँदै नुहाउँछन्।
हिन्दूहरू मलाई मुक्तिका स्वामी भन्छन् र बौद्धहरू सय मूल; नजिकै पानीको छेउमा ज्वाला बलिरहेको छ।

name: Tal Barahi Temple
deity: Goddess Barahi (Varahi), a form of the mother goddess (Ajima)
built_century_text: Local belief dates the shrine to 1669 BS, when King Kulmandan Shah of Kaski is said to have built a thatched hut over a sacred stone on the island. King Mahendra rebuilt it in its current form in 2017 BS; rebuilt again in 2023-2026 after earthquake damage.
dynasty: Shah (Kaski kings); rebuilt under King Mahendra
architecture: Small two-storey pagoda on an island in Phewa Lake, with carved wooden struts, windows and doors and a gilded pinnacle. Wikipedia notes an original stone structure with a two-storey roof; the 2023-26 rebuild used wood and brick in the old form, with Bhaktapur and Lalitpur artisans.
short: A small island pagoda of the goddess Barahi in Phewa Lake, Pokhara's most important religious monument, reached only by boat.
story: Sit still in the boat for a moment as the shore of Lakeside drifts away. Ahead, on a small wooded island in the middle of Phewa Lake, rises the pagoda of Tal Barahi, the most important religious monument in Pokhara. Tal means lake, and Barahi is the mother goddess who is worshipped here as a symbol of female power. Local belief says that a stone on this mound was worshipped as the goddess long before any building stood here, and that King Kulmandan Shah of Kaski first sheltered it under a simple thatched hut. King Mahendra rebuilt the temple in 2017 BS. After the 2015 earthquake left it leaning about three inches to the south, craftsmen from Bhaktapur and Lalitpur rebuilt it again, keeping its old form. Step ashore at the landing, hear the bells and the flapping pigeons, and look back: on a clear morning the Annapurna range floats above the water behind you.
legend: According to local folklore, King Kulmandan Shah of Kaski founded the temple by building a thatched hut over a stone on a mound in the lake, which had been worshipped as the goddess.
facts: The temple stands on a small island in Phewa Lake and can be reached only by boat, about five minutes from Barahi Ghat.
Devotees especially visit in the Nepali months of Baisakh and Kartik.
The 2015 earthquake tilted the temple about three inches to the south.
Reconstruction began in 2080 BS (2023) under the Department of Archaeology at a cost of about NPR 15 million, mostly from devotees' donations.
During reconstruction, worship continued at a silver idol at the nearby Havan Kund.

visit.hours_note: Reached by boat from Barahi Ghat in Lakeside, Pokhara. Opening hours not confirmed in a reliable source.
visit.fee_note: No temple entry fee found; boat fare is paid separately at the ghat.

earthquake_2015: The 2015 earthquake tilted the temple about three inches to the south and left parts submerged. Reconstruction began in 2023 and was reported complete in 2026, with reopening set for Ghatasthapana.

quiz.q_np: कास्कीका कुन राजाले टापुमा पहिलो पटक छाप्रोको मन्दिर बनाएको भनिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: स्थानीय किंवदन्तीले कास्कीका राजा कुलमन्दन शाहलाई पहिलो छाप्रोको श्रेय दिन्छ।

quiz.explanation_np: राजा महेन्द्रले 2017 वि.सं. मा मन्दिर पुनर्निर्माण गरे।

quiz.explanation: Wikipedia notes devotees visit especially in Baisakh and Kartik.

A Kaski king once sheltered a sacred stone here with straw; today a pagoda of the boar-faced mother goddess stands in its place.

short_np: फेवा तालमा रहेको देवी वाराहीको सानो टापु पगोडा, पोखराको सबैभन्दा महत्त्वपूर्ण धार्मिक स्मारक, डुङ्गाबाट मात्र पुगिन्छ।
story_np: लेकसाइडको किनारा टाढा सर्दै जाँदा केही क्षण डुङ्गामा शान्त बस्नुहोस्। अगाडि, फेवा तालको बीचमा रहेको सानो रूखले ढाकेको टापुमा तालबाराहीको पगोडा उभिएको छ, पोखराको सबैभन्दा महत्त्वपूर्ण धार्मिक स्मारक। ताल भनेको सरोवर, र वाराही मातृदेवी हुन् जसलाई यहाँ नारीशक्तिको प्रतीकका रूपमा पूजा गरिन्छ। स्थानीय विश्वासअनुसार यहाँ कुनै भवन बन्नुभन्दा धेरै अघिदेखि यस टिलामा रहेको ढुङ्गालाई देवीका रूपमा पूजा गरिन्थ्यो, र कास्कीका राजा कुलमण्डन शाहले पहिलो पटक त्यसलाई सामान्य छाप्रोमुनि ओत दिएका थिए। राजा महेन्द्रले वि.सं. २०१७ मा मन्दिर पुनर्निर्माण गरे। सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पले यसलाई करिब तीन इन्च दक्षिणतिर ढल्काएपछि, भक्तपुर र ललितपुरका शिल्पीहरूले यसको पुरानै रूप कायम राखेर फेरि पुनर्निर्माण गरे। घाटमा ओर्लनुहोस्, घण्टको आवाज र फड्फडाउने परेवा सुन्नुहोस्, र पछाडि फर्केर हेर्नुहोस्: स्वच्छ बिहान तपाईंको पछाडि पानीमाथि अन्नपूर्ण हिमशृङ्खला तैरिरहेको देखिन्छ।
legend_np: स्थानीय लोककथाअनुसार, कास्कीका राजा कुलमण्डन शाहले तालको टिलामा देवीका रूपमा पूजा गरिएको ढुङ्गामाथि छाप्रो बनाएर मन्दिरको स्थापना गरेका थिए।
facts_np: मन्दिर फेवा तालको सानो टापुमा छ र वाराही घाटबाट करिब पाँच मिनेटमा डुङ्गाबाट मात्र पुगिन्छ।
भक्तजनहरू विशेष गरी नेपाली महिना वैशाख र कार्तिकमा दर्शन गर्न आउँछन्।
सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पले मन्दिरलाई करिब तीन इन्च दक्षिणतिर ढल्कायो।
पुनर्निर्माण वि.सं. २०८० (सन् २०२३) मा पुरातत्त्व विभागको नेतृत्वमा सुरु भयो, करिब १.५ करोड रुपैयाँ लागतमा, अधिकांश भक्तजनको दानबाट।
पुनर्निर्माणका बेला नजिकैको हवन कुण्डमा रहेको चाँदीको मूर्तिमा पूजा जारी रह्यो।
quake_np: सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पले मन्दिरलाई करिब तीन इन्च दक्षिणतिर ढल्कायो र केही भाग पानीमा डुबायो। पुनर्निर्माण सन् २०२३ मा सुरु भई २०२६ मा सम्पन्न भएको बताइएको छ, घटस्थापनामा पुनः खुला गर्ने तय गरिएको छ।
clues_np: अन्नपूर्णको काखको सानो हरियो टापुमा रहेको मेरो ढोकासम्म पुग्न जुत्ता होइन, डुङ्गाको चप्पु चाहिन्छ।
कास्कीका एक राजाले यहाँ पवित्र ढुङ्गालाई पराल ओढाएर जोगाएका थिए; आज त्यही ठाउँमा वराहमुखी माता देवीको प्यागोडा उभिएको छ।

name: Bindhyabasini Temple
deity: Goddess Bindhyabasini, a manifestation of Durga (Yogamaya)
built_century_text: Established around the 1760s; the temple itself is recorded as built in 1842 BS on 47 ropani of land. In June 1815 King Girvan Yuddha Bikram Shah appointed its priest. The present building is a later shikhara rebuild.
architecture: White shikhara-style temple on a hilltop platform, approached by stone stairways from the east, north and south-east. Two golden metal lions flank the gate, and the complex holds shrines to Saraswati, Shiva, Hanuman, Ganesh and Vishnu.
short: One of Pokhara's oldest temples: a white shikhara of goddess Bindhyabasini on a hill in Miruwa, old Pokhara.
story: Climb the stone stairs to this small hill in old Pokhara and you arrive at one of the city's oldest temples. The white shikhara in front of you belongs to Bindhyabasini, a form of Durga. Her story begins in Mathura, where she was born as the baby who escaped the tyrant Kamsa and rose into the sky, later making her home in the Vindhya hills of India. Legend says a king of Kaski, Siddhi Narayan Shah, dreamed of bringing her presence to his kingdom. His envoys carried a statue home from Vindhyachal, but on this hilltop it became impossible to move, so the temple was founded right here. Notice the two golden lions at the gate and the sindoor-red Hanuman by the Ganesh shrine. Around you are shrines to Saraswati, Shiva and Vishnu, and a Sanskrit school. Sadly, Pokhara's great fire of 1949 is said to have started here during an offering.
legend: King Siddhi Narayan Shah of Kaski (or, in other accounts, King Khadgaman Malla of Parbat) dreamed he should bring the goddess from Vindhyachal in India. The statue his envoys carried back could not be lifted again on this hilltop, which was taken as the goddess's chosen home.
facts: The temple is in Ward 2, Miruwa, of Pokhara and is dedicated to Bindhyabasini, a manifestation of Durga.
The temple was established around the 1760s; in 1815 King Girvan Yuddha Bikram Shah appointed its priest.
Most of Pokhara was destroyed in a 1949 fire that allegedly began at the temple during an offering.
A 12-person lift for disabled and elderly pilgrims was inaugurated by the President of Nepal on 7 March 2019.
The complex is managed by the Bindhyabasini Dharmik Chhetra Bikash Samiti.

short_np: पोखराका सबैभन्दा पुराना मन्दिरमध्ये एक: पुरानो पोखराको मिरुवाको डाँडामा बिन्ध्यबासिनी देवीको सेतो शिखर।
story_np: पुरानो पोखराको यो सानो डाँडामा ढुङ्गाका सिँढी चढ्दै जानुभयो भने तपाईं सहरकै सबैभन्दा पुराना मन्दिरमध्ये एकमा पुग्नुहुन्छ। तपाईंको अगाडि रहेको सेतो शिखर दुर्गाको रूप बिन्ध्यबासिनीको हो। उनको कथा मथुराबाट सुरु हुन्छ, जहाँ उनी अत्याचारी कंसबाट बचेर आकाशमा उडेकी बालिकाका रूपमा जन्मिएकी थिइन्, र पछि भारतको विन्ध्य पर्वतमा बसोबास गरिन्। किंवदन्ती अनुसार कास्कीका राजा सिद्धि नारायण शाहले आफ्नो राज्यमा उनको उपस्थिति ल्याउने सपना देखे। उनका दूतहरूले विन्ध्याचलबाट मूर्ति ल्याए, तर यही डाँडामा त्यो सार्नै नसकिने भयो, र यहीँ मन्दिर स्थापना गरियो। ढोकामा रहेका दुई सुनौला सिंह र गणेश मन्दिरछेउको सिन्दुर रङ्गको हनुमान हेर्नुहोस्। वरिपरि सरस्वती, शिव र विष्णुका मन्दिर तथा एउटा संस्कृत विद्यालय छन्। दुःखको कुरा, 1949 को पोखराको ठूलो आगलागी यहीँ चढाउने क्रममा सुरु भएको भनिन्छ।
legend_np: कास्कीका राजा सिद्धि नारायण शाह (वा अर्को वृत्तान्त अनुसार पर्वतका राजा खड्गमान मल्ल) ले भारतको विन्ध्याचलबाट देवीलाई ल्याउनुपर्ने सपना देखे। उनका दूतहरूले फर्काएर ल्याएको मूर्ति यही डाँडामा फेरि उठाउन सकिएन, जसलाई देवीले रोजेको निवास मानियो।
facts_np: मन्दिर पोखराको वडा नं. 2, मिरुवामा छ र दुर्गाको स्वरूप बिन्ध्यबासिनीलाई समर्पित छ।
मन्दिर करिब 1760 को दशकमा स्थापना भएको थियो; 1815 मा राजा गीर्वाणयुद्ध विक्रम शाहले यसका पुजारी नियुक्त गरे।
1949 को आगलागीमा पोखराको धेरैजसो भाग नष्ट भयो, जुन मन्दिरमा चढाउने क्रममा सुरु भएको भनिन्छ।
अपाङ्ग तथा वृद्ध तीर्थयात्रीका लागि 12 जनाको लिफ्ट 7 मार्च 2019 मा नेपालका राष्ट्रपतिले उद्घाटन गरेका थिए।
परिसर बिन्ध्यबासिनी धार्मिक क्षेत्र विकास समितिद्वारा सञ्चालित छ।
clues_np: टाढा पहाडबाट बोकेर ल्याइएको एउटा मूर्तिले पुरानो पोखराको माथिको यो उचाइमा एक पाइला पनि अगाडि बढ्न मानेन।
दुई सुनौला सिंहले मेरो सेतो शिखरको रक्षा गर्छन्, र सन् 1949 मा सहरलाई ढाकेको आगो मेरै वेदीबाट सुरु भएको भनिन्छ।

name: Bhadrakali Temple
built_century_text: Wikipedia and Wikidata give its founding year as 1817 (the calendar era is not stated); the hill was earlier known as Mudule Thumko.
architecture: Small tiered pagoda-roofed shrine with a gilded pinnacle on a brick and stone platform atop a forested hillock, with a Ganesh shrine, a kuti and stone lion guardians in the grounds.
short: A hilltop pagoda of the goddess Bhadrakali in Kundahar, east Pokhara, reached by nearly 300 stone steps through the trees.
story: Count the steps as you climb: from the east there are 292 of them, from the south 265, and both lead you up through green woods to the top of a small hill in Kundahar, on the eastern side of Pokhara. Up here, at about 2,930 feet, stands the temple of Bhadrakali, the goddess of power and strength, a form of Kali and Durga. Before the temple was founded in 1817, people called this hill Mudule Thumko. The story told by devotees is simple and striking: the goddess spoke to a priest and told him to dig into the hill, and there he found her image. Since then she has been worshipped here as Bhadrakali. The temple grounds spread over 135 ropani, with a small Ganesh shrine and a stone lion keeping watch. Come during Dashain and thousands of worshippers fill these quiet paths.
legend: The goddess Bhadrakali told a priest to dig into the hill, where he found her statue; since then it has been worshipped here as Bhadrakali.
facts: The temple stands atop a small hill in Kundahar, east Pokhara, at about 2,930 ft (about 890 m).
The eastern approach has 292 steps and the southern approach 265 steps.
The temple area covers about 135 ropani.
Before the temple was founded, the hill was known as 'Mudule Thumko'.
Dashain is its most important festival, drawing thousands of devotees.

quiz.explanation_np: दशैं यस मन्दिरको सबैभन्दा महत्त्वपूर्ण चाड हो।

short_np: पोखरा पूर्वको कुन्दहारमा रहेको देवी भद्रकालीको डाँडामाथिको पगोडा, रूखहरूबीच करिब 300 ढुङ्गाका भर्‍याङबाट पुगिने।
story_np: उक्लिँदै गर्दा भर्‍याङ गन्नुहोस्: पूर्वबाट 292 वटा छन्, दक्षिणबाट 265 वटा, र दुवैले तपाईंलाई हरिया जङ्गलबीचबाट पोखराको पूर्वी भागमा पर्ने कुन्दहारको सानो डाँडाको टुप्पोसम्म पुर्‍याउँछन्। यहाँ, करिब 2,930 फिटको उचाइमा, शक्ति र बलकी देवी, काली र दुर्गाको एक रूप, भद्रकालीको मन्दिर छ। सन् 1817 मा मन्दिर स्थापना हुनुअघि मानिसहरू यो डाँडालाई मुदुले थुम्को भन्थे। भक्तजनले सुनाउने कथा सरल तर प्रभावशाली छ: देवीले एक पुजारीसँग बोलेर डाँडा खन्न भनिन्, र त्यहाँ उनले देवीको मूर्ति भेटे। त्यसयता यहाँ उनको भद्रकालीका रूपमा पूजा हुन्छ। मन्दिर परिसर 135 रोपनीमा फैलिएको छ, जहाँ एउटा सानो गणेश मन्दिर र ढुङ्गाको सिंहले रखवारी गरिरहेको छ। दशैँमा आउनुहोस्, हजारौँ भक्तजनले यी शान्त बाटाहरू भरिदिन्छन्।
legend_np: देवी भद्रकालीले एक पुजारीलाई डाँडा खन्न भनिन्, जहाँ उनले देवीको मूर्ति भेटे; त्यसयता यहाँ भद्रकालीका रूपमा पूजा गरिँदै आएको छ।
facts_np: मन्दिर पोखरा पूर्वको कुन्दहारमा रहेको सानो डाँडाको टुप्पोमा करिब 2,930 फिट (करिब 890 मिटर) को उचाइमा छ।
पूर्वी बाटोमा 292 वटा र दक्षिणी बाटोमा 265 वटा भर्‍याङ छन्।
मन्दिर क्षेत्र करिब 135 रोपनीमा फैलिएको छ।
मन्दिर स्थापना हुनुअघि यो डाँडा ‘मुदुले थुम्को’ का नामले चिनिन्थ्यो।
दशैँ यसको सबैभन्दा महत्त्वपूर्ण पर्व हो, जसले हजारौँ भक्तजनलाई तान्छ।
clues_np: एक पुजारीले पोखराको पूर्वमा रहेको रुखैरुखले ढाकेको थुम्को खने र भित्र एक उग्र देवी पर्खिरहेकी भेटे।
पूर्वबाट 292 वा दक्षिणबाट 265 सिँढी रोज्नुहोस् र मेरो डाँडामाथिको सानो मन्दिरमा पुग्नुहोस्।

name: Bindebasini Temple, Bandipur
deity: Goddess Bindhyabasini, a form of Durga
built_century_text: Construction date not documented in the sources found; Bandipur bazaar itself grew after Newar traders from Bhaktapur settled here following 1768. The temple was rebuilt after the 2072 BS (2015) earthquake.
architecture: Two-tiered Newar pagoda of brick and carved timber on a stepped base, standing in the stone-paved square at the northern end of Bandipur bazaar, framed by two- and three-storey Newar trading houses with shuttered windows.
short: A Newar pagoda of goddess Bindhyabasini at the head of Bandipur's preserved hilltop trading bazaar in Tanahun.
story: Walk the length of Bandipur's main street, past tall Newar houses with shuttered windows and shops under their verandas, and at the northern end you reach a small square with a pagoda at its heart. This is the temple of Bindhyabasini, a form of Durga. Bandipur was a Magar village until Newar traders from Bhaktapur arrived after Prithvi Narayan Shah conquered the Kathmandu Valley in 1768. Safe from malaria on this saddle of the Mahabharat range, they turned it into a busy stop on the India-Tibet trade route and brought their temples and architecture with them. Look at the carved roof struts and the brickwork, which echo the old pagodas of the valley. The 2015 earthquake damaged the temple, and it has been rebuilt. Locals still come to worship every day, and at the New Year an image of the goddess is pulled through town on a chariot.
facts: Bandipur sits at about 1,030 m on a saddle of the Mahabharat range, some 700 m above the Marsyangdi valley.

The temple stands in the square at the northern end of Bandipur bazaar.
It was rebuilt after the 2072 BS (2015) earthquake.
Since 1998 Bandipur has been linked by an 8 km road from Dumre on the Prithvi Highway.

short_np: तनहुँको बन्दिपुरको संरक्षित डाँडाको व्यापारिक बजारको शिरमा रहेको देवी बिन्ध्यबासिनीको नेवारी पगोडा।
story_np: बन्दिपुरको मुख्य सडकको लम्बाइमा हिँड्नुहोस्, झ्यालमा ढोका भएका अग्ला नेवारी घर र तिनका बरन्डामुनिका पसलहरू पार गर्दै, र उत्तरी छेउमा तपाईं एउटा सानो चोकमा पुग्नुहुन्छ जहाँ बीचमा पगोडा छ। यो दुर्गाको रूप बिन्ध्यबासिनीको मन्दिर हो। सन् १७६८ मा पृथ्वीनारायण शाहले काठमाडौं उपत्यका जितेपछि भक्तपुरका नेवार व्यापारीहरू आउनुअघि बन्दिपुर मगर गाउँ थियो। महाभारत श्रृङ्खलाको यो भञ्ज्याङमा मलेरियाको डर नभएकाले उनीहरूले यसलाई भारत-तिब्बत व्यापार मार्गको व्यस्त विश्रामस्थल बनाए र आफ्ना मन्दिर र वास्तुकला साथै ल्याए। कुँदिएका छानाका टेको र इँटाको काम हेर्नुहोस्, जसले उपत्यकाका पुराना पगोडाहरूको झल्को दिन्छन्। सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पले मन्दिरलाई क्षति पुर्‍यायो, र यसलाई पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको छ। स्थानीयहरू अझै हरेक दिन पूजा गर्न आउँछन्, र नयाँ वर्षमा देवीको मूर्तिलाई रथमा राखेर सहरभरि तानिन्छ।
facts_np: बन्दिपुर करिब १,०३० मिटरमा महाभारत श्रृङ्खलाको भञ्ज्याङमा अवस्थित छ, मर्स्याङ्दी उपत्यकाभन्दा करिब ७०० मिटर माथि।

name: Khadga Devi Temple
deity: Khadga Devi, goddess of the sacred sword
built_century_text: Construction date not documented in the sources found. The sword kept here is believed to have belonged to the 16th-century king Mukunda Sen.
architecture: Two-storey red-brick shrine with a pitched tiled roof topped by a small lantern and pinnacle, entered up a short flight of stone steps; set in a wide open ground with rest houses (pati) and large pipal trees above Bandipur bazaar.
short: Hilltop shrine above Bandipur bazaar that guards a sacred sword said to have belonged to King Mukunda Sen, paraded at Dashain.
story: Climb a little above Bandipur's old bazaar and the houses give way to a wide open ground, shaded by great pipal trees. The red-brick shrine in front of you is the home of Khadga Devi, the goddess of the sword. Khadga means sword, and the treasure kept here is a blade believed to have belonged to Mukunda Sen, a king of the 16th century; tradition says it was a gift from Lord Shiva himself. For most of the year the doors stay shut. They open on Fulpati, during Dashain, when the town holds its Khadga Jatra. Then members of the Magar and Bishwokarma communities carry the sacred sword in procession through the streets, and Hindu devotees come to worship it. The temple is especially important to Bandipur's Newar Shrestha families. Stand by the pati, the old rest house, look out over the ridge, and imagine the drums and the flash of steel on festival day.
legend: The sword kept in the temple is believed to have belonged to King Mukunda Sen and to have been a gift from Lord Shiva.
facts: Khadga Jatra, held during Dashain, centres on a religious service at the Khadga Devi temple.
Magar and Bishwokarma communities parade a sacred sword through Bandipur during the jatra.
The sword is believed to have belonged to King Mukunda Sen.
The temple opens only on Fulpati, one day of the Dashain festival.

short_np: बन्दीपुर बजारमाथिको डाँडामा रहेको मन्दिर, जसले राजा मुकुन्द सेनको भनिएको पवित्र खड्ग जोगाएको छ र दशैँमा यसको यात्रा गरिन्छ।
story_np: बन्दीपुरको पुरानो बजारभन्दा अलि माथि उक्लनुहोस् र घरहरू ठूला पिपलका रूखले छाया पारेको खुला चौरमा परिणत हुन्छन्। तपाईंको अगाडिको रातो इँटाको मन्दिर तरवारकी देवी खड्गदेवीको थलो हो। खड्ग भनेको तरवार, र यहाँ राखिएको निधि सोह्रौं शताब्दीका राजा मुकुन्द सेनको भनिएको तरवार हो; परम्परा अनुसार यो स्वयं भगवान् शिवको उपहार थियो। वर्षको अधिकांश समय ढोका बन्द रहन्छ। दशैँको फूलपातीमा ढोका खुल्छ, जब सहरले खड्ग जात्रा मनाउँछ। तब मगर र विश्वकर्मा समुदायका मानिसहरूले पवित्र तरवार सडकमा जुलुस गर्दै लैजान्छन्, र हिन्दू भक्तजनहरू पूजा गर्न आउँछन्। मन्दिर बन्दीपुरका नेवार श्रेष्ठ परिवारहरूका लागि विशेष महत्त्वको छ। पुरानो पाटी, विश्राम गृहको छेउमा उभिनुहोस्, भञ्ज्याङतिर हेर्नुहोस्, र उत्सवको दिनका ढोल र फलामको चमकको कल्पना गर्नुहोस्।
legend_np: मन्दिरमा राखिएको तरवार राजा मुकुन्द सेनको हो र भगवान् शिवको उपहार हो भन्ने विश्वास छ।
facts_np: दशैँमा हुने खड्ग जात्रा खड्गदेवी मन्दिरको धार्मिक पूजामा केन्द्रित हुन्छ।
जात्राका बेला मगर र विश्वकर्मा समुदायले पवित्र तरवारलाई बन्दीपुरभर जुलुस गराउँछन्।
तरवार राजा मुकुन्द सेनको हो भन्ने विश्वास छ।
मन्दिर दशैँ पर्वको एक दिन, फूलपातीमा मात्र खुल्छ।
गर्भगृहमा खड्गमाईको मूर्ति छ, र नजिकै पाटी र ठूला पिपलका रूखहरू छन्।
clues_np: ठूलो शरद् चाडको एक दिन मात्र मेरा ढोका खुल्छन्, जब एक पुराना राजाको तरबार सडकभर डुलाइन्छ।
नेवार बजारमाथिका ठूला पीपलका रूखमुनि एउटी देवीले शिवको उपहार मानिने हतियार राखेकी छन्।

name: Lo Manthang Walled City
alt_names: Capital of the Kingdom of Lo
coord_source: Wikidata P625 of Lo Manthang Palace (Q105753160), at the centre of the walled city
built_century_text: Founded in 1380 by Ame Pal, first king of Lo, who built the city wall; the four-storey royal palace is dated to 1440. Thubchen and Jampa Lhakhang monasteries date from the 15th century.
dynasty: Kings of Lo (Bista line descended from Ame Pal)
architecture: Compact fortified town of whitewashed and ochre mud-brick houses inside a rammed-earth and stone wall entered by one gate. The nine-cornered royal palace is of mud, stone and wood; red-walled Thubchen (37.2 x 24 m, 12 m high, 35 wooden pillars) and Jampa Lhakhang hold 15th-century murals.
short: The 14th-century walled capital of the Kingdom of Lo in Upper Mustang, with a royal palace and 15th-century painted monasteries.
story: Pass through the single gate in this earthen wall and you are inside the capital of a kingdom that lasted more than six hundred years. Ame Pal, the warrior who founded the Kingdom of Lo, built this walled city in 1380, and his descendants ruled from here until Nepal became a republic in 2008. Around you are whitewashed houses with firewood stacked on their flat roofs, narrow alleys, and above them the many-cornered royal palace. Now look for the great red walls of the monasteries. Thubchen Lhakhang, from the 15th century, is held up by thirty-five wooden pillars, and its murals glow with turquoise, malachite and gold. Jampa Lhakhang, the Maitreya temple, holds what is said to be the world's largest collection of painted mandalas. Outside the wall stretch green barley fields in a desert of eroded cliffs. Upper Mustang was closed to outsiders until 1992, and foreigners still need a special permit to come here.
facts: Lo Manthang was founded in 1380 by Ame Pal, who oversaw construction of the city wall.
The last raja of Mustang, Jigme Dorje Palbar Bista, lost his title when Nepal became a republic in 2008.
Jampa Lhakhang contains what is described as the world's largest collection of mandalas painted on its walls.
Upper Mustang was closed to outsiders until 1992; foreigners need a special permit costing US$500 for ten days.
The royal palace, damaged in 2015, was restored with help from the Gerda Henkel Foundation by 2073 BS.

visit.hours_note: Remote high-altitude town (about 3,800 m) reached by jeep road or multi-day trek from Jomsom; monastery opening times vary.
visit.fee_note: Foreigners need an Upper Mustang restricted-area permit: US$500 for ten days, then US$50 per day (Wikipedia). Monastery fees not confirmed.

earthquake_2015: The April 2015 earthquake damaged the royal palace, later restored with the Gerda Henkel Foundation, and severely damaged the 500-year-old wall paintings of Jampa Lhakhang.

short_np: माथिल्लो मुस्ताङमा रहेको लो राज्यको चौधौँ शताब्दीको गढीबन्द राजधानी, जहाँ राजदरबार र पन्ध्रौँ शताब्दीका चित्रित गुम्बा छन्।
story_np: यो माटाको पर्खालको एक मात्र ढोकाबाट छिर्नुभयो भने तपाईं छ सय वर्षभन्दा बढी टिकेको एउटा राज्यको राजधानीभित्र पुग्नुहुन्छ। लो राज्यका संस्थापक योद्धा अमे पालले 1380 मा यो गढीबन्द सहर बनाए, र 2008 मा नेपाल गणतन्त्र नहुँदासम्म उनका सन्ततिले यहींबाट शासन गरे। तपाईंको वरिपरि सपाट छानामा दाउरा थुपारिएका सेता घर, साँघुरा गल्ली र तिनमाथि धेरै कुना भएको राजदरबार छन्। अब गुम्बाका ठूला रातो पर्खाल खोज्नुहोस्। पन्ध्रौँ शताब्दीको थुबचेन ल्हाखाङ पैँतीसवटा काठका स्तम्भमा अडिएको छ, र यसका भित्तेचित्र फिरोजा, मलाकाइट र सुनले झिलिमिली छन्। मैत्रेय मन्दिर जम्पा ल्हाखाङमा संसारकै सबैभन्दा ठूलो चित्रित मण्डलको सङ्ग्रह रहेको भनिन्छ। पर्खाल बाहिर खिइएका पहाडी भीरका मरुभूमिमा हरिया जौका खेत फैलिएका छन्। माथिल्लो मुस्ताङ 1992 सम्म बाहिरीहरूका लागि बन्द थियो, र विदेशीहरूलाई अझै पनि यहाँ आउन विशेष अनुमतिपत्र चाहिन्छ।
facts_np: लोमान्थाङ 1380 मा अमे पालले स्थापना गरेका थिए, जसले सहरको पर्खाल निर्माणको निरीक्षण गरे।
मुस्ताङका अन्तिम राजा जिग्मे दोर्जे पल्बार बिस्टाले 2008 मा नेपाल गणतन्त्र हुँदा आफ्नो उपाधि गुमाए।
जम्पा ल्हाखाङमा यसका भित्तामा चित्रित मण्डलहरूको संसारकै सबैभन्दा ठूलो सङ्ग्रह रहेको वर्णन गरिन्छ।
माथिल्लो मुस्ताङ 1992 सम्म बाहिरीहरूका लागि बन्द थियो; विदेशीहरूलाई दस दिनका लागि US$500 पर्ने विशेष अनुमतिपत्र चाहिन्छ।
2015 मा क्षति भएको राजदरबार गेर्डा हेन्केल फाउन्डेसनको सहयोगमा 2073 BS सम्ममा पुनर्स्थापना गरियो।
quake_np: सन् 2015 अप्रिलको भूकम्पले राजदरबारमा क्षति पुर्‍यायो, जुन पछि गेर्डा हेन्केल फाउन्डेसनको सहयोगमा पुनर्स्थापना गरियो, र जम्पा ल्हाखाङका 500 वर्ष पुराना भित्तेचित्रमा गम्भीर क्षति पुर्‍यायो।
clues_np: मेरो एक मात्र ढोकाबाट भित्र पस, अनि हिमालयको हराएको राज्यको माटोले बनेको राजधानी भेट्नेछौ, जहाँ छ शताब्दीसम्म एउटै वंशले शासन गर्‍यो।
मेरा रातो मन्दिरहरूले पन्ध्रौँ शताब्दीका भित्ते चित्र र हजार जति चित्रित मण्डल लुकाएका छन्, सन् 1992 मा पर्यटकका लागि खुलेको बन्द भूमिमा।

name: Kagbeni and Kag Chode Monastery
built_century_text: Kag Chode Thupten Samphel Ling monastery was founded in 1429 CE, credited to the monk Tenpai Gyaltsen; its old wing is described as about 500 years old. The ruined Kag Khar fort-palace is older by local tradition.
architecture: Red-painted Tibetan-style gompa of rammed earth and timber on a spur above the Kali Gandaki, with an old wing and a newer building. The village is a tight cluster of flat-roofed mud-brick houses, chortens, and the four-storey adobe ruin of Kag Khar.
short: Medieval fortified village at the gate of Upper Mustang, crowned by the red 15th-century Sakya monastery of Kag Chode.
story: Welcome to Kagbeni, a village of mud-brick houses and narrow tunnels at the meeting of two rivers, where the Kali Gandaki valley opens towards the old Kingdom of Lo. Beni means confluence, and pilgrims bound for Muktinath stop on these stony banks; Hindu families perform shraddha rites here for their ancestors. Look up at the blood-red walls on the spur above the river. That is Kag Chode Thupten Samphel Ling, a Sakya monastery founded in 1429 and remembered as the work of the monk Tenpai Gyaltsen. Its rammed-earth walls were built to resist both earthquakes and attackers. Nearby stand the crumbling adobe towers of Kag Khar, the old palace of a local king. At the village gates, look for the kheni, carved male and female guardians called ghost eaters, who replaced human sentries long ago. North of here begins Upper Mustang, where foreign visitors need a special permit to continue.
legend: The kheni, a pair of male and female carved figures at the village gates, are believed to guard Kagbeni against evil and supernatural forces, earning them the name 'ghost eaters'.
facts: Kag Chode Thupten Samphel Ling, the 'Red Monastery', was founded in 1429 and belongs to the Sakya tradition.
Kagbeni lies in the Kali Gandaki valley, on the trail from Jomsom to Lo Manthang near the turn to Muktinath.
Foreign visitors need a special Upper Mustang permit to travel north of Kagbeni.
The 2011 census counted 555 people in the village.
An August 2023 flood on the Kagbeni river damaged the area and threatened the monastery.

visit.hours_note: Village on the Jomsom-Muktinath road, high in the Kali Gandaki valley; monastery visiting hours not confirmed.
visit.fee_note: Kagbeni is within the Annapurna Conservation Area; travel north of the village needs the Upper Mustang permit. Monastery fee not confirmed.

short_np: माथिल्लो मुस्ताङको प्रवेशद्वारमा रहेको मध्यकालीन किल्लाबन्दी गाउँ, जसको टुप्पोमा पन्ध्रौँ शताब्दीको रातो सक्य गुम्बा कागचोदे छ।
story_np: कागबेनीमा स्वागत छ, माटोका इँटाका घर र साँघुरा सुरुङ भएको गाउँ, जहाँ दुई नदीको सङ्गममा कालीगण्डकी उपत्यका प्राचीन लो राज्यतर्फ खुल्छ। बेनी भनेको सङ्गम हो, र मुक्तिनाथतर्फ जाने तीर्थयात्रीहरू यी ढुङ्गैले भरिएका किनारमा रोकिन्छन्; हिन्दू परिवारहरूले यहाँ आफ्ना पितृहरूका लागि श्राद्ध गर्छन्। नदीमाथिको डाँडाका ढाडमा रहेका रगतजस्ता रातो पर्खालतिर हेर्नुहोस्। त्यो कागचोदे थुप्तेन साम्फेल लिङ हो, सन् 1429 मा स्थापित सक्य गुम्बा, जसलाई भिक्षु तेन्पाई ग्यल्चेनको काम भनी सम्झिइन्छ। यसका कुटेको माटोका पर्खाल भूकम्प र आक्रमणकारी दुवैको प्रतिरोध गर्न बनाइएका थिए। नजिकै कागखर, स्थानीय राजाको पुरानो दरबारका भत्किँदै गरेका माटोका धुरीहरू छन्। गाउँका ढोकामा खेनी खोज्नुहोस्, कुँदिएका पुरुष र महिला संरक्षक, जसलाई भूतभक्षक भनिन्छ र जसले धेरै पहिले मानव पहरेदारको ठाउँ लिए। यहाँबाट उत्तरतिर माथिल्लो मुस्ताङ सुरु हुन्छ, जहाँ विदेशी पर्यटकलाई अघि बढ्न विशेष अनुमतिपत्र चाहिन्छ।
legend_np: गाउँको ढोकामा रहेका पुरुष र महिलाका कुँदिएका जोडी मूर्ति खेनीले कागबेनीलाई दुष्ट र अलौकिक शक्तिबाट जोगाउँछन् भन्ने विश्वास गरिन्छ, जसले उनीहरूलाई ‘भूतभक्षक’ नाम दिएको हो।
facts_np: ‘रातो गुम्बा’ भनिने कागचोदे थुप्तेन साम्फेल लिङ सन् 1429 मा स्थापना भएको थियो र सक्य परम्परासँग सम्बन्धित छ।
कागबेनी कालीगण्डकी उपत्यकामा, मुक्तिनाथतिर मोडिने ठाउँनजिक, जोमसोमबाट लो मन्थाङ जाने बाटोमा पर्छ।
कागबेनीभन्दा उत्तर यात्रा गर्न विदेशी पर्यटकलाई माथिल्लो मुस्ताङको विशेष अनुमतिपत्र चाहिन्छ।
सन् 2011 को जनगणनाले गाउँमा 555 जना गणना गरेको थियो।
सन् 2023 को अगस्टमा कागबेनी खोलामा आएको बाढीले क्षेत्रमा क्षति पुर्‍यायो र गुम्बालाई जोखिममा पार्‍यो।
clues_np: भूत खाने उपनाम पाएका माटोका रक्षकहरूले मेरा ढोका कुरेका छन्, जहाँबाट यात्रीहरू कुनै बेला निषेधित राज्यतर्फ उत्तर लाग्थे।
मेरो रगतजस्तो रातो गुम्बा 1429 देखि नदीहरू मिल्ने ठाउँमाथि उभिएको छ, र तीर्थयात्रीहरू सय धाराको बाटोमा यहाँ विश्राम गर्छन्।

name: Galeshwor Dham
deity: Shiva as Galeshwor, a self-manifested jyotirlinga
built_century_text: Worship at the site is described as ancient; the date of the present temple building is not documented in the sources found. A donor gilded its pinnacle (gajur) in Mangsir 2082 BS (2025).
architecture: Two-tiered pagoda-roofed Shiva temple standing on a single huge rock of about three ropani at the river's edge, with stone steps down to the water and a narrow rock pool beside it whose level is said to stay constant all year.
short: Riverside Shiva shrine on a great rock where the Rahughat meets the Kali Gandaki, north of Beni: the 'gateway to Muktinath'.
story: Listen to the rivers. Here, about three kilometres north of Beni, the Rahughat stream rushes into the grey Kali Gandaki, and on a single enormous rock at their meeting stands Galeshwor, a temple of Shiva. Inside is a jyotirlinga believed to be swayambhu, self-manifested. The name comes from a legend: as Shiva carried the body of his wife Sati towards the Himalaya, her neck, gala in Nepali, fell here and took the form of Shiva. That is why pilgrims call this place the gateway to Muktinath; many stop here before heading up the Kali Gandaki valley. Beside the temple, between the rocks, lies a long narrow pool. People say it never dries in winter and never overflows in the monsoon. On Maha Shivaratri, crowds start gathering at four in the morning, coming from Myagdi, Baglung, Mustang, Parbat and Kaski to light a great lamp and offer prayers. In late 2025 a donor gilded the temple's pinnacle.
legend: While Shiva carried the body of Sati towards the Himalaya, her neck (gala) fell at this spot and took the form of Shiva; hence the name Galeshwor, 'Lord of the neck'.
facts: Galeshwor lies about 3 km north of Beni, the headquarters of Myagdi district, in Beni Municipality ward 9.
The temple stands where the Rahughat (Rahu) river joins the Kali Gandaki.
It is known as the gateway to Muktinath and is visited by both Hindus and Buddhists.
More than 50,000 devotees were expected on Maha Shivaratri 2081 BS, according to the local development fund.
The pool beside the temple is said to keep the same water level all year round.

visit.hours_note: Beside the Beni-Jomsom road; daily worship is held. Opening hours not documented.
visit.fee_note: No entry fee found in sources.

quiz.q: To which god is Galeshwor dedicated?
quiz.explanation: Galeshwor is a Shiva shrine with a self-manifested jyotirlinga.
quiz.q_np: गलेश्वर कुन देवतालाई समर्पित छ?
quiz.explanation_np: गलेश्वर स्वयम्भू ज्योतिर्लिङ्ग भएको शिव मन्दिर हो।

quiz.explanation: The temple stands at the confluence of the Rahughat river and the Kali Gandaki.
quiz.q_np: गलेश्वरको छेउबाट कुन ठूलो नदी बग्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: मन्दिर राहुघाट खोला र कालीगण्डकीको सङ्गममा अवस्थित छ।

quiz.q: According to legend, which part of Sati's body fell here?
quiz.explanation: Gala means neck; Sati's neck is said to have fallen here, giving the name Galeshwor.
quiz.q_np: किंवदन्ती अनुसार सतीको शरीरको कुन अङ्ग यहाँ खस्यो?
quiz.explanation_np: गला भनेको घाँटी हो; सतीको घाँटी यहाँ खसेको भनिन्छ, जसबाट गलेश्वर नाम रहेको हो।

quiz.q: Galeshwor is popularly called the gateway to which pilgrimage site?
quiz.explanation: Pilgrims stop here on the way up the Kali Gandaki to Muktinath.
quiz.q_np: गलेश्वरलाई लोकप्रिय रूपमा कुन तीर्थस्थलको प्रवेशद्वार भनिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: कालीगण्डकी माथि मुक्तिनाथ जाने तीर्थयात्रीहरू यहाँ रोकिन्छन्।

quiz.q: What is unusual about the pool beside the temple, according to locals?
options: Its level stays the same all year
quiz.explanation: The pool reportedly neither dries in winter nor fills completely in the monsoon.

short_np: बेनी उत्तरमा राहुघाट र कालीगण्डकीको संगमस्थलको विशाल चट्टानमाथिको नदीकिनारको शिव मन्दिर: 'मुक्तिनाथको प्रवेशद्वार'।
story_np: नदीहरूलाई सुन्नुहोस्। यहाँ, बेनीको करिब तीन किलोमिटर उत्तरमा, राहुघाट खोला खैरो कालीगण्डकीमा मिसिन्छ, र तिनीहरूको मिलनस्थलको एउटै विशाल चट्टानमाथि शिवको मन्दिर गलेश्वर उभिएको छ। भित्र स्वयम्भू, अर्थात् आफैँ प्रकट भएको, मानिने ज्योतिर्लिङ्ग छ। नाम एउटा कथाबाट आएको हो: शिवले आफ्नी पत्नी सतीको शव बोकेर हिमालतर्फ जाँदा, उनको गर्धन, नेपालीमा गला, यहाँ खस्यो र शिवको रूप धारण गर्‍यो। त्यसैले तीर्थयात्रीहरू यस ठाउँलाई मुक्तिनाथको प्रवेशद्वार भन्छन्; धेरैजना कालीगण्डकी उपत्यकातर्फ माथि जानुअघि यहाँ रोकिन्छन्। मन्दिरको छेउमा, चट्टानहरूका बीचमा, एउटा लामो साँघुरो पोखरी छ। मानिसहरू भन्छन् यो जाडोमा कहिल्यै सुक्दैन र वर्षामा कहिल्यै उर्लिँदैन। महाशिवरात्रिमा बिहान चार बजेदेखि नै म्याग्दी, बाग्लुङ, मुस्ताङ, पर्वत र कास्कीबाट आएका भक्तजनहरूको भीड जम्न थाल्छ, ठूलो दीप बाल्न र प्रार्थना गर्न। सन् २०२५ को अन्त्यतिर एक दाताले मन्दिरको गजुरमा सुन पानी चढाए।
legend_np: शिवले सतीको शव बोकेर हिमालतर्फ जाँदा, उनको गर्धन (गला) यही ठाउँमा खस्यो र शिवको रूप लियो; त्यसैले यसको नाम गलेश्वर, 'गर्धनका स्वामी', पर्‍यो।
facts_np: गलेश्वर म्याग्दी जिल्लाको सदरमुकाम बेनीको करिब ३ कि.मी. उत्तरमा, बेनी नगरपालिका वडा ९ मा अवस्थित छ।
मन्दिर राहुघाट (राहु) खोला कालीगण्डकीमा मिसिने ठाउँमा छ।
यो मुक्तिनाथको प्रवेशद्वारका रूपमा चिनिन्छ र हिन्दू तथा बौद्ध दुवैले यसको दर्शन गर्छन्।
स्थानीय विकास कोषका अनुसार महाशिवरात्रि २०८१ साल मा ५०,००० भन्दा बढी भक्तजन आउने अपेक्षा गरिएको थियो।
मन्दिरको छेउको पोखरीमा वर्षभरि पानीको सतह उही रहन्छ भनिन्छ।
clues_np: यस नदी सङ्गममा एक देवीको घाँटी खसेको भनिन्छ, र अहिले एउटा विशाल चट्टानमाथि शिवको मन्दिर छ।
मुस्ताङका सय मूल जाने तीर्थयात्री पहिले मकहाँ रोकिन्छन्, म म्याग्दीको सदरमुकामभन्दा अलि उत्तरमा छु।

name: Devghat Dham
deity: Shiva and Vishnu (Harihar); Vishnu worshipped as Shaligram
built_century_text: An ancient pilgrimage site; the start of its Makar Sankranti bathing fair is unknown. Its many temples, ashrams and the suspension bridge are of various modern dates.
architecture: A riverside pilgrimage town of small Hindu temples, ashrams, caves and bathing ghats along the meeting of the Trishuli and Kali Gandaki, joined across the river by a long suspension bridge linking Tanahun and Chitwan.
short: Sacred confluence of the Trishuli and Kali Gandaki near Narayangadh, famed for its Maghe Sankranti bathing fair.
story: Stand on the stone steps and watch two great rivers become one. From the north-west comes the Kali Gandaki, which began near Muktinath; from the north-east comes the Trishuli, fed by Gosaikunda. Here at Devghat they meet and flow on together as the Narayani. Hindus call this place Harihar Kshetra, holy to both Shiva and Vishnu, and they search the gravel for Shaligram stones, worshipped as Vishnu himself. The sage Vasistha is said to have made his ashram here, and you will find temples, quiet ashrams and even a cave linked to the goddess Sita. Many elderly Hindus come to spend their last years beside these waters. Cross the swaying suspension bridge and you step from Tanahun into Chitwan. If you come on Maghe Sankranti in January, join the crowd: hundreds of thousands of pilgrims bathe at the confluence in one of the largest melas in Nepal. Nobody knows when this festival began.
legend: The sage Vasistha is believed to have established his ashram and performed his austerities at Devghat.
facts: Devghat lies at the confluence of the Trishuli and Kali (Krishna) Gandaki rivers, about 7 km from Narayangadh.
Below the confluence the combined river is known as the Narayani.
Its Makar (Maghe) Sankranti mela is one of the largest religious fairs in Nepal; one report estimated over three lakh visitors.
A historic suspension bridge links the Tanahun and Chitwan sides of the town.
Pilgrims bathe and seek Shaligram stones, which Hindus worship as Vishnu.

visit.hours_note: Open riverside pilgrimage area reached by bus or taxi from Narayangadh (about 7 km).
visit.fee_note: No entry fee found in sources.

quiz.explanation_np: मकर (माघे) सङ्क्रान्तिको मेला नेपालकै सबैभन्दा ठूला मेलामध्ये एक हो।

quiz.q_np: कालीगण्डकीमा पाइने पवित्र ढुङ्गालाई के भनिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: शालिग्राम ढुङ्गालाई विष्णुका रूपमा पूजा गरिन्छ।

quiz.q: What is the river called below the Devghat confluence?
quiz.explanation: After the confluence the combined river is called the Narayani.
quiz.q_np: देवघाटको सङ्गमपछि नदीलाई के भनिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: सङ्गमपछि मिलेको नदीलाई नारायणी भनिन्छ।

quiz.q: Which sage is said to have had his ashram at Devghat?
quiz.explanation: Sage Vasistha is believed to have established his ashram and done tapasya here.
quiz.q_np: कुन ऋषिले देवघाटमा आश्रम बनाएको भनिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: ऋषि वशिष्ठले यहाँ आश्रम स्थापना गरी तपस्या गरेको विश्वास गरिन्छ।

clues: A river from Mustang and a river from Gosaikunda meet below my steps, and a swinging bridge joins two districts.
In the month of Magh, pilgrims crowd my banks to bathe where Shiva and Vishnu are honoured together.

short_np: नारायणगढ नजिक त्रिशूली र कालीगण्डकीको पवित्र सङ्गम, माघे सङ्क्रान्तिको स्नान मेलाका लागि प्रसिद्ध।
story_np: ढुङ्गाका भर्‍याङमा उभिएर दुई विशाल नदी एक हुँदै गरेको हेर्नुहोस्। उत्तर-पश्चिमबाट मुक्तिनाथ नजिकबाट सुरु भएको कालीगण्डकी आउँछ; उत्तर-पूर्वबाट गोसाइँकुण्डले पोषित त्रिशूली आउँछ। यहाँ देवघाटमा तिनीहरू भेटिन्छन् र नारायणीका रूपमा सँगै बग्छन्। हिन्दूहरूले यस ठाउँलाई हरिहर क्षेत्र भन्छन्, शिव र विष्णु दुवैका लागि पवित्र, र तिनीहरू विष्णु स्वयंका रूपमा पूजिने शालिग्राम ढुङ्गा खोज्न गिट्टीमा खोज्छन्। ऋषि वशिष्ठले यहीँ आफ्नो आश्रम बनाएको भनिन्छ, र तपाईंले यहाँ मन्दिर, शान्त आश्रम र देवी सीतासँग जोडिएको गुफा पनि भेट्टाउनुहुनेछ। धेरै वृद्ध हिन्दूहरू आफ्नो अन्तिम वर्ष यी पानीको छेउमा बिताउन आउँछन्। हल्लिने झोलुङ्गे पुल तरेर तपाईं तनहुँबाट चितवनमा पुग्नुहुन्छ। जनवरीमा माघे सङ्क्रान्तिमा आउनुभयो भने भीडमा सामेल हुनुहोस्: लाखौँ तीर्थयात्री सङ्गममा नुहाउँछन्, नेपालका सबैभन्दा ठूला मेलाहरूमध्ये एकमा। यो मेला कहिले सुरु भयो भन्ने कसैलाई थाहा छैन।
legend_np: ऋषि वशिष्ठले देवघाटमा आफ्नो आश्रम स्थापना गरी तपस्या गरेका थिए भन्ने विश्वास छ।
facts_np: देवघाट त्रिशूली र काली (कृष्ण) गण्डकी नदीको सङ्गममा, नारायणगढबाट करिब ७ किमी टाढा छ।
सङ्गमपछि दुवै नदी मिलेर बग्ने नदीलाई नारायणी भनिन्छ।
यहाँको मकर (माघे) सङ्क्रान्तिको मेला नेपालका सबैभन्दा ठूला धार्मिक मेलाहरूमध्ये एक हो; एउटा प्रतिवेदनले तीन लाखभन्दा बढी आगन्तुकको अनुमान गरेको थियो।
ऐतिहासिक झोलुङ्गे पुलले सहरको तनहुँ र चितवन पट्टिलाई जोड्छ।
तीर्थयात्रीहरू नुहाउँछन् र शालिग्राम ढुङ्गा खोज्छन्, जसलाई हिन्दूहरू विष्णुका रूपमा पूजा गर्छन्।
clues_np: मुस्ताङबाट आएको एउटा नदी र गोसाइँकुण्डबाट आएको अर्को नदी मेरा भर्‍याङमुनि मिल्छन्, र एउटा झोलुङ्गे पुलले दुई जिल्ला जोड्छ।
माघ महिनामा, जहाँ शिव र विष्णु सँगै पूजिन्छन्, मेरा किनारमा नुहाउन तीर्थयात्रीको भीड लाग्छ।

name: Siddha Cave
deity: Shiva (rock formations venerated as his symbols; small shrine inside)
built_century_text: A natural limestone (karst) cave. Local lore says a woman collecting herbs found it in 1989; German speleologists explored and surveyed it in 1990 and 1991.
architecture: Natural karst cave in layered limestone, entered from a forested slope above the Prithvi Highway. Wikipedia gives it 437 m deep and 50 m high; showcaves.com records 758 m of passages and 105 m vertical range. Stalactites and stalagmites fill the chambers.
short: Huge limestone cave above Bimalnagar on the trail to Bandipur, full of stalactites and venerated by Shiva pilgrims.
story: Switch on your headlamp and let your eyes adjust. You are inside Siddha Gufa, one of the largest caves in Nepal, which opens high on the hillside above Bimalnagar, on the old trail up to Bandipur. Local lore says a woman gathering herbs stumbled on the entrance in 1989, and German cave explorers mapped it in 1990 and 1991. Wikipedia gives its depth as 437 metres and its height as about 50 metres, enough room, it is said, for 2,500 people. Look at the walls: layers of brown and white limestone, and formations that guides compare to an elephant, snake heads, butterflies and turtles. For pilgrims, these shapes are signs of Shiva, and a small shrine stands inside, along with a shelter where meditators sometimes stay. Listen too; clusters of bats hang in the darkness above you. Watch your step on the slippery path and ladders, and come back out to daylight and the green Marsyangdi hills.
legend: Pilgrims regard the cave's rock formations as natural symbols of Shiva, and the cave has long been used by meditators, as its name 'Siddha' (an accomplished ascetic) suggests.
facts: Wikipedia gives the cave a depth of 437 m and a height of 50 m, with room for about 2,500 people.
Local lore says it was found in 1989 by a woman collecting herbs; German speleologists surveyed it in 1990-91.
Showcaves.com lists 758 m of passages and a vertical range of 105 m, calling it Nepal's deepest known cave.
The entrance is about 30 minutes' walk uphill from Bimal Bazaar on the Prithvi Highway.
Bats roost inside, and there is a small Shiva shrine.

visit.hours_note: Open daily all year 10:00-17:00 (showcaves.com, 2025 information). The path inside is dark and slippery; helmet and headlamp are provided.
visit.fee_note: NPR 100 per adult plus NPR 100 for a compulsory guide (showcaves.com, 2025); the Kathmandu Post reported Rs 200 for a guided tour in 2019. No separate rate for foreigners found.

quiz.q: What kind of heritage site is Siddha Gufa?
quiz.explanation: Siddha Gufa is a natural karst cave in limestone.
quiz.q_np: सिद्ध गुफा कस्तो सम्पदा स्थल हो?
quiz.explanation_np: सिद्ध गुफा चूनढुङ्गामा बनेको प्राकृतिक कार्स्ट गुफा हो।

quiz.q: Near which highway bazaar is the cave's trailhead?
quiz.explanation: The cave is about 30 minutes' walk up from Bimal Bazaar on the Prithvi Highway.
quiz.q_np: गुफामा पुग्ने बाटो कुन राजमार्गको बजार नजिकबाट सुरु हुन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: पृथ्वी राजमार्गको बिमल बजारबाट गुफा करिब 30 मिनेट उकालो हिँडेपछि पुगिन्छ।

quiz.q: Which animals cluster on the cave walls?
quiz.explanation: Clusters of bats cling to the walls inside.
quiz.q_np: गुफाका भित्तामा कुन जनावरहरू झुम्मिएर बस्छन्?
quiz.explanation_np: भित्र भित्तामा चमेराका समूह झुण्डिएका हुन्छन्।

quiz.q: To which god are the cave's formations and shrine dedicated?
quiz.explanation: Pilgrims treat the formations as symbols of Shiva, and a small Shiva shrine stands inside.
quiz.q_np: गुफाका आकृति र मन्दिर कुन देवतालाई समर्पित छन्?
quiz.explanation_np: तीर्थयात्रीहरूले आकृतिहरूलाई शिवका प्रतीक मान्छन्, र भित्र सानो शिव मन्दिर छ।

quiz.q: According to local lore, in which year was the cave discovered?
quiz.explanation: A woman collecting herbs is said to have found it in 1989; it was surveyed in 1990-91.
quiz.q_np: स्थानीय कथन अनुसार गुफा कुन वर्ष भेटिएको थियो?
quiz.explanation_np: जडीबुटी टिप्न गएकी एक महिलाले सन् 1989 मा भेटेको भनिन्छ; 1990-91 मा सर्वेक्षण गरिएको थियो।

clues: A herb gatherer stumbled on my dark mouth in 1989, halfway up the trail to a Newar hill town.
Bring a torch: inside me, stone elephants, snake heads and turtles hang from the roof among sleeping bats.

model.notes: Dark mouth in a mossy limestone cliff reached by steep stairs, opening into a vast brown-and-cream chamber hung with stalactites.

short_np: बन्दीपुरको बाटोमा बिमलनगरमाथि रहेको विशाल चुनढुङ्गाको गुफा, जहाँ स्ट्यालाक्टाइटहरू छन् र शिवभक्त तीर्थयात्रीहरूले पूज्छन्।
story_np: आफ्नो हेडल्याम्प बाल्नुहोस् र आँखालाई अँध्यारोमा अभ्यस्त हुन दिनुहोस्। तपाईं सिद्ध गुफाभित्र हुनुहुन्छ, नेपालका सबैभन्दा ठूला गुफामध्ये एक, जुन बन्दीपुर जाने पुरानो बाटोमा बिमलनगरमाथिको पहाडमा खुल्छ। स्थानीय भनाइ अनुसार 1989 मा जडीबुटी टिप्दै गरेकी एक महिलाले संयोगले यसको मुख भेटिन्, र जर्मन गुफा अन्वेषकहरूले 1990 र 1991 मा यसको नक्सा बनाए। विकिपिडियाले यसको गहिराइ 437 मिटर र उचाइ करिब 50 मिटर दिएको छ, जहाँ 2,500 मानिस अटाउन सक्छन् भनिन्छ। पर्खालमा हेर्नुहोस्: खैरो र सेतो चुनढुङ्गाका तह, र गाइडहरूले हात्ती, सर्पका टाउका, पुतली र कछुवासँग तुलना गर्ने आकृतिहरू। तीर्थयात्रीका लागि यी आकृति शिवका चिन्ह हुन्, र भित्र एउटा सानो मन्दिर छ, साथै ध्यानीहरू कहिलेकाहीँ बस्ने आश्रय पनि। सुन्नुहोस् पनि; माथिको अँध्यारोमा चमेरा झुन्डिएका छन्। चिप्लो बाटो र भर्‍याङमा होसियार भई हिँड्नुहोस्, र उज्यालोमा तथा हरिया मर्स्याङ्दीका डाँडामा फर्कनुहोस्।
legend_np: तीर्थयात्रीहरू गुफाका चट्टानी आकृतिलाई शिवका प्राकृतिक प्रतीक मान्छन्, र यसको नाम 'सिद्ध' (सिद्धि प्राप्त तपस्वी) ले संकेत गरेझैं गुफा लामो समयदेखि ध्यानीहरूले प्रयोग गर्दै आएका छन्।
facts_np: विकिपिडियाले गुफाको गहिराइ 437 मिटर र उचाइ 50 मिटर दिएको छ, जहाँ करिब 2,500 मानिस अटाउन सक्छन्।
स्थानीय भनाइ अनुसार यो 1989 मा जडीबुटी सङ्कलन गर्दै गरेकी एक महिलाले भेटेकी थिइन्; जर्मन गुफा विशेषज्ञहरूले 1990-91 मा यसको सर्वेक्षण गरे।
Showcaves.com ले 758 मिटर मार्ग र 105 मिटर ठाडो दायरा सूचीबद्ध गर्दै यसलाई नेपालको ज्ञात सबैभन्दा गहिरो गुफा भनेको छ।
पृथ्वी राजमार्गको बिमल बजारबाट गुफाको प्रवेशद्वार उकालो करिब 30 मिनेटको पैदल दूरीमा छ।
भित्र चमेराहरू बस्छन्, र एउटा सानो शिव मन्दिर छ।
clues_np: एक जडीबुटी टिप्ने मानिस सन् 1989 मा नेवार पहाडी बस्तीतर्फको बाटोको आधा दूरीमा मेरो अँध्यारो मुखमा ठोक्किए।
टर्च लिएर आऊ: मभित्र छतबाट ढुङ्गाका हात्ती, सर्पका टाउका र कछुवा सुतिरहेका चमेराका बीचमा झुण्डिएका छन्।

name: Kalika Bhagawati Temple
built_century_text: Founded, according to local folklore, by King Pratap Narayan Singh Malla of Parbat after his marriage to a daughter of King Manimukunda Sen; no firm construction date is documented in the sources found.
architecture: Three-tiered red pagoda with a broad lower roof over an ambulatory, set in a paved courtyard with entrances on all four cardinal sides, surrounded by smaller shrines to Shiva, Radha Krishna and Lakshmi Narayan inside a protected guthi forest.
short: Baglung's great Kali temple, a three-tiered pagoda in a sacred forest above the Kali Gandaki, famed for its Chaite Dashain fair.
story: Step into the shade of the forest on the edge of Baglung bazaar and you will find a courtyard with four gateways, one for each direction. At its centre rises the red three-tiered pagoda of Kalika Bhagawati, the fierce goddess Kali. The story of this place begins with a wedding. King Pratap Narayan Singh Malla of Parbat married the daughter of King Manimukunda Sen and received an image of Kalika as part of her dowry. On the way home the wedding party sheltered in this forest for the night. In the morning, no one could lift the idol, so the king built a temple on the spot. Around you are smaller shrines to Shiva, Radha Krishna and Lakshmi Narayan. Come in Chaitra for Chaite Dashain, when thousands light oil lamps and some couples even marry here for the goddess's blessing. Since April 2016 pigeons are no longer sacrificed; they are set free instead.
legend: King Pratap Narayan Singh Malla of Parbat received the goddess's idol as dowry from King Manimukunda Sen. When his wedding party rested overnight in this forest, the idol could not be moved the next morning, so he built the temple there.
facts: The temple stands south-east of Baglung town, above the Kali Gandaki River.
Its courtyard has four entrances, one in each cardinal direction.
Chaite Dashain, on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Chaitra, is its biggest festival.
On 13 April 2016 pigeon sacrifice was stopped; pigeons are now released in the temple grounds.
The temple is surrounded by the protected Kalika Bhagawati Guthi Forest.

visit.hours_note: Next to Baglung bazaar; opening hours not documented in the sources found.
visit.fee_note: No entry fee found in sources.

quiz.q: Which goddess is worshipped at this Baglung temple?
quiz.explanation: The presiding deity is Kalika, a fierce form of Shakti.
quiz.q_np: बागलुङको यस मन्दिरमा कुन देवीको पूजा गरिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: मुख्य देवी कालिका हुन्, जो शक्तिको उग्र रूप हुन्।

quiz.q: How many entrances does the temple courtyard have?
quiz.explanation: The courtyard has four entrances, one in each cardinal direction.
quiz.q_np: मन्दिरको चोकमा कति ओटा प्रवेशद्वार छन्?
quiz.explanation_np: चोकमा चार दिशामा एक-एक गरी चार प्रवेशद्वार छन्।

quiz.q: In which Nepali month is the main festival, Chaite Dashain, held?
quiz.explanation: Chaite Dashain falls on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Chaitra.
quiz.q_np: मुख्य चाड चैते दशैं नेपाली कुन महिनामा मनाइन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: चैते दशैं चैत्र शुक्ल पक्षको अष्टमीका दिन पर्छ।

quiz.q: How did the king of Parbat receive the goddess's image, according to folklore?
quiz.explanation: Pratap Narayan Singh Malla received it in the dowry of Manimukunda Sen's daughter.
quiz.q_np: लोककथा अनुसार पर्वतका राजाले देवीको मूर्ति कसरी पाए?
quiz.explanation_np: प्रताप नारायण सिंह मल्लले मणिमुकुन्द सेनकी छोरीको दाइजोमा यो पाएका थिए।

quiz.q: Which offering was stopped at the temple in April 2016?
quiz.explanation: Pigeon sacrifice ended on 13 April 2016 because the pigeon symbolises peace.
quiz.q_np: अप्रिल 2016 मा मन्दिरमा कुन चढाउने चलन बन्द गरियो?
quiz.explanation_np: परेवा शान्तिको प्रतीक भएकाले 13 अप्रिल 2016 मा परेवाको बलि बन्द गरियो।

clues: A goddess who arrived as a bride's dowry refused to leave the forest where the wedding party camped.
Four gates lead to my red three-roofed pagoda beside a Kali Gandaki bazaar; in Chaitra, couples marry here for blessings.

festivals.name: Chaite Dashain
festivals.note: Main festival on Chaitra Shukla Ashtami; devotees light oil lamps, perform puja and some marry here.
festivals.note_np: चैत्र शुक्ल अष्टमीका दिन मनाइने मुख्य चाड; भक्तजनले तेलका बत्ती बाल्छन्, पूजा गर्छन् र कसैकसैले यहीँ विवाह गर्छन्।

festivals.name: Dashain
festivals.note: Celebrated from the bright fortnight of Ashwin to the full moon.

short_np: बागलुङको ठूलो कालिका मन्दिर, कालीगण्डकीमाथिको पवित्र वनभित्रको तीनतले पगोडा, चैते दशैँ मेलाका लागि प्रसिद्ध।
story_np: बागलुङ बजारको छेउको जङ्गलको छायाँमा पस्नुहोस् र चारै दिशाका लागि एक-एक वटा गरी चार ढोका भएको आँगन भेट्नुहुनेछ। यसको बीचमा उग्र देवी काली कालिका भगवतीको रातो तीनतले पगोडा उभिएको छ। यस ठाउँको कथा एउटा विवाहबाट सुरु हुन्छ। पर्वतका राजा प्रताप नारायण सिंह मल्लले राजा मणिमुकुन्द सेनकी छोरीसँग विवाह गरे र दाइजोको अंशका रूपमा कालिकाको मूर्ति पाए। घर फर्किने बाटोमा जन्ती यही जङ्गलमा रात बिताउन रोकिए। बिहान कसैले मूर्ति उठाउन सकेनन्, त्यसैले राजाले त्यही ठाउँमा मन्दिर बनाए। तपाईंको वरिपरि शिव, राधाकृष्ण र लक्ष्मीनारायणका साना मन्दिरहरू छन्। चैत्रमा चैते दशैँमा आउनुहोस्, जब हजारौँ मानिसले तेलका बत्ती बाल्छन् र केही जोडीले देवीको आशीर्वादका लागि यहीँ विवाह पनि गर्छन्। सन् 2016 को अप्रिलदेखि परेवाको बलि दिइँदैन; बरु तिनलाई स्वतन्त्र छोडिन्छ।
legend_np: पर्वतका राजा प्रताप नारायण सिंह मल्लले राजा मणिमुकुन्द सेनबाट दाइजोमा देवीको मूर्ति पाए। उनको जन्ती यही जङ्गलमा रातभर आराम गर्दा भोलिपल्ट बिहान मूर्ति हल्लाउन सकिएन, त्यसैले उनले त्यहीँ मन्दिर बनाए।
facts_np: मन्दिर बागलुङ सहरको दक्षिणपूर्वमा, कालीगण्डकी नदीमाथि छ।
यसको आँगनमा चार प्रवेशद्वार छन्, प्रत्येक दिशामा एक-एक।
चैत्र शुक्ल पक्षको अष्टमीमा पर्ने चैते दशैँ यसको सबैभन्दा ठूलो पर्व हो।
सन् 2016 को अप्रिल 13 मा परेवाको बलि बन्द गरियो; अब परेवा मन्दिर परिसरमा छोडिन्छन्।
मन्दिर संरक्षित कालिका भगवती गुठी वनले घेरिएको छ।
clues_np: दाइजोमा आएकी एक देवीले जन्ती बास बसेको जङ्गल छोड्न मानिनन्।
चार ढोकाले मेरो रातो तीन छाने पगोडासम्म पुर्‍याउँछन्, जुन कालीगण्डकी किनारको एउटा बजारछेउ छ; चैतमा जोडीहरू आशीर्वाद लिन यहाँ विवाह गर्छन्।

name: Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave
deity: Shiva (Gupteshwor Mahadev, 'the hidden lord'), worshipped as a lingam
built_century_text: A natural karst cave, reported discovered in 1950; the staircase entrance was built in 1991. It was first surveyed by Tony Waltham's British Karst Research Expedition, and a second British expedition studied its animals in 1976.
architecture: Natural cave in Pokhara conglomerate entered down a spiral concrete stairway, with a shrine chamber holding a Shiva lingam behind metal bars; a lower passage descends about 20 m to the Pardi Khola behind Devi's Fall. Showcaves.com gives 2,950 m length and 48 m vertical range.
short: A Shiva cave shrine in Chhorepatan, Pokhara, whose lower passage lets you see Devi's Fall plunging from behind.
story: Wind your way down the spiral stairway at Chhorepatan and the noise of the city fades into the echo of rushing water. You are entering Gupteshwor Mahadev, the cave of the hidden Lord Shiva. In the first chamber, protected behind metal bars, stands the lingam that pilgrims come to worship, perhaps shaped by nature itself as a stalagmite. People here say the cave was found in 1950, and the entrance stairs you just used were built in 1991. If the season allows, keep going down. A damp, narrow passage drops about twenty metres to the river, and suddenly you are standing behind Devi's Fall, the waterfall across the road, watching the water of Phewa Lake thunder past in the darkness. British cave researchers came here in the 1970s to map the passages and to count its residents, including great leaf-nosed bats and fruit bats. Hold the railing and enjoy the cool air.
facts: The cave lies in Pokhara-17, Chhorepatan, opposite Devi's (Davis) Fall.
Water from Devi's Fall, the outflow of Phewa Lake (Pardi Khola), passes through the cave.
Showcaves.com reports it was discovered in 1950 and its entrance staircase was built in 1991.
A 1976 British expedition recorded great Himalayan leaf-nosed bats and fruit bats living inside.
Showcaves.com lists the cave as about 2,950 m long with a vertical range of 48 m.

visit.hours_note: Cave temple open daily; the deeper cave behind it was reported open October-May and closed in the June-September monsoon (showcaves.com, 2010 data).
visit.fee_note: Showcaves.com (2010 data) listed Rs 30 for the temple and Rs 100 for the cave behind; current fees not confirmed.

quiz.q: Which god is worshipped inside Gupteshwor Cave?
quiz.explanation: Gupteshwor Mahadev means the hidden Lord Shiva; a Shiva lingam is worshipped inside.
quiz.q_np: गुप्तेश्वर गुफाभित्र कुन देवताको पूजा गरिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: गुप्तेश्वर महादेव भनेको लुकेका भगवान् शिव हुन्; भित्र शिवलिङ्गको पूजा गरिन्छ।

quiz.q: Which famous waterfall can be seen from inside the cave?
quiz.explanation: A lower passage leads behind Devi's Fall (Patale Chhango), across the road.
quiz.q_np: गुफाभित्रबाट कुन प्रसिद्ध झरना देख्न सकिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: तल्लो बाटोले सडकको पारि रहेको देवीको झरना (पाताले छाँगो) को पछाडिसम्म पुर्‍याउँछ।

quiz.q: In which part of Pokhara is the cave?
quiz.explanation: The cave is in Pokhara-17, Chhorepatan.
quiz.q_np: गुफा पोखराको कुन भागमा छ?
quiz.explanation_np: गुफा पोखरा-17, छोरेपाटनमा छ।

quiz.q: In which year was the entrance staircase built?
quiz.explanation: Showcaves.com records the staircase at the entrance as built in 1991.
quiz.q_np: प्रवेशद्वारको भर्‍याङ कुन वर्षमा बनाइएको थियो?
quiz.explanation_np: Showcaves.com ले प्रवेशद्वारको भर्‍याङ 1991 मा बनेको भनी उल्लेख गरेको छ।

quiz.q: Which river, draining Phewa Lake, flows through the cave?
quiz.explanation: Wikipedia notes the river draining Phewa Tal through the cave is the Pardi Khola.
quiz.q_np: फेवा तालको निकास भएर गुफाभित्र बग्ने नदी कुन हो?
quiz.explanation_np: विकिपिडियाका अनुसार फेवा तालबाट निस्केर गुफाभित्र बग्ने खोला पर्दी खोला हो।

clues: Spiral down beneath a busy road to meet a hidden lord, then keep going to watch a famous waterfall from behind.
The outflow of a big lake vanishes into the ground opposite me, and I let pilgrims see where it goes.

story_np: छोरेपाटनको घुमाउरो भर्‍याङबाट तल झर्दै जानुहोस् र सहरको कोलाहल बगिरहेको पानीको गुञ्जनमा हराउँछ। तपाईं गुप्तेश्वर महादेव, लुकेका शिवको गुफामा प्रवेश गर्दै हुनुहुन्छ। पहिलो कोठामा, फलामको जालीभित्र, तीर्थयात्रीहरू पूजा गर्न आउने शिवलिङ्ग छ, सायद प्रकृतिले नै स्तम्भका रूपमा आकार दिएको। यहाँका मानिसहरू भन्छन् गुफा सन् १९५० मा भेटिएको थियो, र तपाईंले अहिले प्रयोग गर्नुभएको प्रवेशको भर्‍याङ सन् १९९१ मा बनाइएको थियो। मौसमले दिएमा, तल जान जारी राख्नुहोस्। एउटा चिसो, साँघुरो बाटो करिब बीस मिटर तल नदीसम्म झर्छ, र अचानक तपाईं सडकपारिको झरना, देवीको झरना, को पछाडि उभिनुहुन्छ, अँध्यारोमा फेवा तालको पानी गर्जिँदै बगेको हेर्दै। सन् १९७० को दशकमा बेलायती गुफा अनुसन्धानकर्ताहरू यहाँ बाटाहरूको नक्सा बनाउन र ठूला पात-नाके चमेरा र फल खाने चमेरा लगायतका बासिन्दाहरू गन्न आएका थिए। रेलिङ समात्नुहोस् र चिसो हावाको आनन्द लिनुहोस्।
facts_np: गुफा पोखरा-१७, छोरेपाटनमा, देवी (डेविस) फल्सको अगाडि पर्छ।
फेवा तालको निकास (पर्दी खोला) देवीको झरनाको पानी गुफाभित्र भएर बग्छ।
Showcaves.com का अनुसार यो सन् १९५० मा पत्ता लागेको थियो र यसको प्रवेशको भर्‍याङ सन् १९९१ मा बनाइएको थियो।
सन् १९७६ को बेलायती अभियानले भित्र बस्ने ठूला हिमाली पात-नाके चमेरा र फल खाने चमेराहरू दर्ज गरेको थियो।
Showcaves.com ले गुफाको लम्बाइ करिब २,९५० मिटर र ठाडो दायरा ४८ मिटर रहेको उल्लेख गरेको छ।
clues_np: व्यस्त सडकमुनि घुमाउरो बाटो झरेर लुकेका भगवान्‍लाई भेट, अनि अझै अगाडि बढेर एउटा प्रसिद्ध झरनालाई पछाडिबाट हेर।
एउटा ठूलो तालको निकास मेरो अगाडिपट्टि जमिनमुनि हराउँछ, र म तीर्थयात्रीलाई त्यो कहाँ जान्छ भनेर देखाउँछु।
